diagram_math_checks.objects_and_maps: GrMod_0(A) -> GrMod_0(B) by Be tensor_A(-); GrMod_0(B) -> GrMod_0(A) by e(-).
checks: Be has left B multiplication and right A multiplication through iota; these commute and e acts as identity on its right. Therefore Be tensor_A X is a graded left B-module for any graded left A-module X, exactly the upper left-to-right arrow. For the displayed external tensor input, X=M tensor_k N; no claim that every A-module is external is made.

eB has left A multiplication through iota and right B multiplication. For a graded left B-module L, eL is a graded left A-module via iota; the lower arrow is right-to-left. No inverse-equivalence or commutative square is asserted.

The restriction tensor map eB tensor_B L -> eL, eb tensor l |-> ebl, is balanced since (eb bprime)l=eb(bprime l); it is A-linear and degree zero. Its inverse sends v in eL to e tensor v. Composites give ev=v and e tensor ebl=eb tensor l by balancing and e^2=e. This checks the explanatory tensor identification directly.

For degree-zero maps f:X->Xprime and g:L->Lprime, induction uses 1 tensor f and restriction uses g restricted to eL; both preserve the stated domains and gradings. The total degree and outer action conventions agree with the local balanced-tensor definition.
